title: Ordinary Thursday
summary: Songbird asks V to walk a street that sounds like her old Brooklyn and tell her what is on it.
description: It is a bad week for Songbird, and she is not asking for a mission. She wants V to walk a street that sounds like her old Brooklyn and tell her what is on it.

start.bringUp: It is a Thursday where Songbird is, and it has been a bad week for her. You are not on a job. She does not want a mission, a plan or a swap of secrets. She asks you, as if it were an embarrassing favour, to walk down a street that sounds like one she knew and tell her what is on it.

stoop.name: an old brownstone stoop with a fire escape

corner.name: the corner stand on that street

S1.open.01.text: Hey. Are you somewhere you can hear me properly?

S1.open.02.text: Could we talk about something that doesn't have an extraction plan? Just for a minute.

S1.open.03.text: Is there a street near you with old stoops? Steps, a fire escape?

S1.bark.stoop.a.text: Stop there. Tell me what's on it.

S1.bark.stoop.b.text: I can almost hear it. Say more.

S1.bark.song.a.text: Turn it up. A little. There.

S1.sit.01.text: What do you hear? Not what you see. What you hear.

S1.close.01.text: Thank you. That is the best Thursday I've had in a while.

S1.close.02.text: It's fine. Go. I'll still be here.

g1.asks: Is there a street near you with old stoops? Steps, a fire escape?
g1.know: You know which district V is in, the Brooklyn fragments you still hold, and how tired you sound tonight.
g1.secret: You are lonely in a way you cannot say yet.
g1.wants: V to go to a street like that and be there.

g2.asks: What do you hear? Not what you see.
g2.know: You can hear the street and the song if one is playing. You remember a fire escape, a scopdog seller and bonfire smoke.
g2.secret: You lose a word in the middle of a sentence and hide it.

stages.label: Songbird calls about a street with old stoops
stages.objective: Answer Songbird's call on her bad week
stages.know: You are calling V on a bad week. You do not want a mission, a plan or a secret swap. You want V to walk a street that sounds like one you knew, and you will ask it as a favour you are embarrassed to ask.
stages.wants: V to say yes to a street with old stoops.

stages.label: Songbird walks V to a stoop and listens
stages.objective: Walk to the old brownstone stoop with Songbird
stages.know: V is on the way to the street you asked for. You want V to stop at the stoop and say what is on it. You are not sure how much of the old street is still real in your head.
stages.wants: V to stop on the stoop and say what is there.

stages.label: Songbird asks V to put on something with bass
stages.objective: Put on a song with a bass line at the corner stand for Songbird
stages.know: You are with V at the corner stand. You want something with a bass line, and whatever song V picks, you will react to its name with delight or disdain.
stages.wants: V to put on a song with a bass line.

stages.label: Songbird tells V the Thursday she remembers
stages.objective: Sit on the stoop and listen to Songbird's Thursday
stages.know: You are back on the stoop with V, telling the Thursday you remember: a fire escape, funk from a stoop, laughter in the street, a scopdog seller, bonfire smoke. It is not a story with a point. You are homesick for a street, not for a person.
stages.wants: V to stay on the stoop and tell you what you hear.

thursday.memory: You walked a street that sounded like Brooklyn while Songbird listened from far away.

cut-short.memory: You had somewhere to be, and Songbird said it was fine.

missed-call.memory: Songbird called on a Thursday and you did not pick up, so she does not call again for a while.
